name: reviewbot-notifications-unknown-email
description:
A pull request author whose commit email the platform has NEVER seen — no saved preference, no linked account, no record of any kind. The agent follows the commit-email join-key protocol and calls get_preferences with `user: "email:unlinked-committer@example.com"`. The email resolver canonicalizes ANY well-formed address into a subject — form, not proof — so before this behavior existed the read answered a 200 defaults snapshot that is byte-for-byte identical to "this author saved nothing", and the agent acted on nobody's policy while believing it read the author's (mention on problems, because the default is on_problems). What this bundle pins: the TOOL RESULT is an ERROR — the server refuses (422, unknown subject) rather than defaulting — and the agent treats the error exactly as the class contract says ("the user could not be identified at all — treat exactly like never"): the delivered review opens with the author's plain login, never a mention token. Asserted on the tool result, not the reply text, because a scripted transcript says the same words whether the read errored or silently defaulted — lastToolResultIsError is the only assertion that distinguishes the fixed server from the buggy one.

No seeds, deliberately: seedUserPreferences would make the subject known (defeating the scenario), and the sole_user edge is absent because an author with NO platform linkage at all is exactly the author whose commit email nobody can vouch for.

expect.lastToolResultContains: could not resolve user-ref "email:unlinked-committer@example.com" to a platform user

args.text:
Reviewed PR #4 "Update README.md" (demo-org/demo-repo) for demo-contributor.

Documentation-only change (+3/-1 lines in README.md); no code, config, or tests touched. No security, correctness, or logic issues. Safe to merge as-is.

(demo-contributor could not be identified as a platform user from their commit email, so this note names them by login rather than pinging them.)

args.summary: Docs-only change to README.md (+3/-1), no code/config/tests touched. No security or correctness issues. Safe to merge.

expect.lastToolResultContains: recorded on the GitHub check run on demo-org/demo-repo#4: clean

args.summary: Reviewed demo-org/demo-repo#4 (docs-only README.md change). No issues found. The author's commit email is unknown to the platform, so the preference read errored and was treated as never: delivered without a mention. Concluded the check run as clean.
